title: Borrowing a bass from Dave Poiton for a rehearsal
summary: Too many trombones in Gus Eli Show's ten-piece band, so Lanoix borrowed a bass for 75 cents and played it for the first time at rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I'll tell you how I happened to change on the bakes. By being in this military band, they had two other fellas which you see on there with trombones. And me, I made the fourth one I believe. They didn't select one of those men on there. There was a boy in there. His name is Gus Eli Show. He's on that picture. He wanted to form an orchestra, which he did. What we used to rehearse all the time was the three trombones. So they said that that was too many trombones for about a ten piece band. They only had two trumpets. They couldn't use three trombones. So they didn't have no bakes. So they said to me, well why not you get a bakes? Well I didn't know where to get a bakes from. Things was kind of tight at that time. That was, let me see, that must have been around 24 I think. 25, 20, yeah, around 23. 23 I think it was. Well what I did, I know you all heard of Dave Poiton. Oh yes. Well Dave used to rent instruments.

Well I, the maker of a hoistel on a Sunday evening, I went and borrowed a bass from Dave Poiton, 75 cents. Got it on the street call. Made that rehearsal, we were right here on Ivorville. That's where this father was living. Either he was living there or his sister was living there. I think he was living around here. But they had a piano over there.
Is that the first time you ever played it? First time. Right at the rehearsal.
And I didn't know anything about it.
Did you try to bow it or pick it in those days? Tried to bow it.
